title: Security FAQ accuracy: audit log fields, retention controls, and export tooling references
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Context
- This ticket was opened during the regulated workloads ABM pilot after multiple prospects (Brightline Insurance, Regal Wealth, NorthBridge Bank) asked for: (a) the exact audit log fields we emit today, (b) how long logs are retained by default vs configurable options, and (c) how audit logs can be exported into their SIEM/storage.
- Sales is currently linking the Confluence “Regulated Workloads Security FAQ” in outbound and during security reviews. We need to ensure the FAQ is precise and matches current product behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Goal
- Confirm and document (internally, for Sales/Security enablement) the current audit log schema and retention behavior.
- Update internal pointers/links in the Security FAQ and evidence pack index so Sales is sending the right artifacts.
- Provide a small, compliance-safe reference config/snippet for Private deployments showing supported export destinations (without over-claiming integrations).

In scope
1) Audit log fields (current state)
- Validate the canonical set of fields emitted by:
  - Control plane actions (admin/user actions in Console/API)
  - Data plane inference requests (generation/embeddings/rerank) where applicable
  - Auth events (SSO/SAML/SCIM provisioning events where available)
- Produce an “approved field list” (and explicit exclusions) for Security/Sales.

2) Retention controls (current state)
- Confirm default retention for audit logs per deployment mode:
  - Hosted API
  - Dedicated
  - Private (VPC / on-prem package)
- Confirm what is configurable today (by plan/add-on) vs what requires a custom engagement.
- Confirm whether “0 retention” / “customer-managed retention only” is supported in Private (and what the actual operational constraints are).

3) Export tooling references
- Confirm what export mechanisms are supported for Private deployments today, and which are “pattern supported” (customer-managed collectors) vs “first-class” supported.
- Ensure docs avoid naming specific SIEM vendors unless we have a tested integration guide.

4) Update internal docs pointers used by Sales
- Update links in the Confluence Security FAQ and evidence pack index to point to:
  - The latest internal schema reference (this ticket output)
  - The example snippet/config in the redwood-examples repo
  - The correct “how to request evidence” process

Out of scope
- Implementing new audit log fields, building new export connectors, or changing retention behavior. If we discover gaps, we’ll open follow-up product/eng tickets.

Acceptance criteria
- A single internal note (in this ticket) that enumerates:
  - Audit log field list (by event type) + definitions
  - Deployment-mode differences (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
  - Retention defaults + what’s configurable today
  - Export options in Private (supported/patterns)
  - “Do not claim” statements for Sales (to prevent overreach)
- Security sign-off from Dr. Aisha Rahman or Naomi Feldman on externally referenced wording.
- Docs pointers updated (tracked via linked PRs/tickets).

Confirmed: Audit log field list (as of 2025-06-04)
Note: Field availability varies by event type and deployment mode. Not all fields apply to every record.

A) Common fields (present on all audit events)
- event_time: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC)
- event_id: unique identifier
- event_type: categorical (see below)
- actor_type: user | service_account | system
- actor_id: internal identifier (redacted/hashed in some exported views)
- actor_email: present for user actions where available (may be omitted in Private if customer config disables email collection)
- org_id / tenant_id
- environment_id (where applicable)
- source_ip: client IP when available
- user_agent: for Console/API control-plane events when available
- auth_context: method indicator (e.g., api_key, oauth, saml) when available
- outcome: success | failure
- failure_reason: populated for failures when safe to emit

B) Control plane / admin events (Console + Management API)
Event types include:
- auth.login
- auth.logout
- auth.sso.assertion
- identity.scim.user_created
- identity.scim.user_updated
- identity.scim.user_deprovisioned
- access.api_key_created
- access.api_key_revoked
- access.role_assigned
- access.role_revoked
- config.model_version_pinned
- config.routing_policy_updated
- config.retention_policy_updated
- export.audit_export_target_created
- export.audit_export_target_updated
- export.audit_export_target_deleted
Additional fields (when applicable):
- resource_type (e.g., api_key, user, role, routing_policy)
- resource_id
- request_id (control plane)

C) Data plane inference request events (availability depends on deployment mode/config)
Event types include:
- inference.request
- inference.response
- inference.error
Additional fields (when applicable):
- request_id (data plane)
- model_id
- model_version
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- region
- latency_ms
- http_status
- token_usage.prompt_tokens (if computed)
- token_usage.completion_tokens (if computed)
- token_usage.total_tokens (if computed)

Explicit exclusions / reminders for Sales & Security
- We do not log raw prompt content or raw model outputs in audit logs by default.
- For Private deployments, customers can optionally configure additional application logging on their side; Redwood’s audit logs are designed for access/configuration/inference metadata, not content capture.
- Token usage fields may be omitted if the request path does not compute them or if customer config disables usage attribution in logs.

Retention behavior (confirmed with Security + Private deployments)
- Hosted API:
  - Default retention: 30 days for audit logs in the standard plan (subject to contract/plan).
  - Extended retention is available as an enterprise add-on; exact duration is contract-defined.
- Dedicated:
  - Default retention: 30 days.
  - Extended retention is available via enterprise add-on; contract-defined.
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Default retention: customer-controlled within the deployment. Redwood does not require long-term retention in the control plane; customers can configure retention to align to their policy.
  - Practical constraint: short-term buffering is required for reliable delivery (e.g., transient queue/buffer). This is an operational setting, not “retention for audit/compliance purposes.”

“Do not claim” guidance (approved)
- Do not claim “HIPAA compliant” or “HIPAA certified.” Use “supports private deployments and controls commonly required for PHI-adjacent workloads; customers configure to meet their compliance obligations.”
- Do not claim “immutable/WORM audit logs” unless explicitly contracted and implemented for the customer’s storage layer.
- Do not name specific SIEM vendors as “supported integrations” unless using the phrase “exportable to customer-managed SIEM via supported export targets.”

Export options for Private deployments (confirmed)
- First-class export targets (supported configuration):
  - HTTPS endpoint (customer-managed collector)
  - S3-compatible object storage (customer-managed bucket)
- Pattern-supported (customer implements collector/bridge):
  - Syslog forwarding via customer agent
  - SIEM ingestion via customer-managed connectors (e.g., forwarding from object storage or HTTP collector)
